concept.title: Renaming based on multiple ditavalref elements
concept.shortdesc: It is possible for a branch with ditavalref already in effect to specify an additional ditavalref, where each ditavalref includes renaming metadata.

conbody.p: When resource renaming metadata is specified at multiple levels of a branch, the prefixes and suffixes are combined. Values specified by a more deeply nested ditavalref element appear closer to the original resource name.

example.p: For example, the following code sample has two ditavalref elements with resource renaming metadata at different levels of the same branch:
example.codeblock: <topicref href="branchParent.dita"> <ditavalref href="parent.ditaval"> <ditavalmeta> <dvrResourcePrefix>parentPrefix-</dvrResourcePrefix> </ditavalmeta> </ditavalref> <!-- additional topics or layers of nesting --> <topicref href="branchChild.dita"> <ditavalref href="child.ditaval"> <ditavalmeta> <dvrResourcePrefix>childPrefix-</dvrResourcePrefix> </ditavalmeta> </ditavalref> <!-- ... --> </topicref> </topicref>
example.p: In this situation, the resource branchChild.dita is given a prefix based on both the reference to parent.ditaval and the reference to child.ditaval. The value childPrefix- is specified in the ditavalref that is nested more deeply within the branch, so it appears closer to the original resource name. The resource branchChild.dita would result in parentPrefix-childPrefix-branchChild.dita. Suffixes (if specified) would be added in a similar manner, resulting in a name like branchChild-childSuffix-parentSuffix.dita. Note that the hyphens in these examples are part of the specified prefix and suffix values; they are not added automatically.
In the following example, metadata in the ditavalref is used to rename key scopes rather than resources.
example.codeblock: <topicref href="branchParent.dita" keyscope="branchscope"> <ditavalref href="parent.ditaval"> <ditavalmeta> <dvrKeyscopePrefix>parentPrefix-</dvrKeyscopePrefix> </ditavalmeta> </ditavalref> <!-- additional topics or layers of nesting --> <topicref href="branchChild.dita"> <ditavalref href="child.ditaval"> <ditavalmeta> <dvrKeyscopePrefix>childscope</dvrKeyscopePrefix> </ditavalmeta> </ditavalref> <!-- ... --> </topicref> </topicref>
example.p: In this example, the scope name branchscope is modified with a key scope prefix to make parentPrefix-branchscope. The child branch has no authored keyscope attribute, so the key scope prefix at that level creates a new scope named childscope. This scope is nested within the scope parentPrefix-branchscope, creating the qualified scope name parentPrefix-branchscope.childscope that can be used to reference keys defined inside of that child branch.
